correctness.rationale: For any selected original edge set A, its odd-degree vertices S induce exact parity identity |A union Odd_{L(H)}(A)|=|delta_H(S)|+|A without delta_H(S)|. Every nontrivial even-shore cut with at most five support is a four-edge cut isolating a pair under cubicity, girth five and cyclic five-connectivity. A parity case analysis shows the only proper-cut equality sets are singleton edges; S empty gives exactly five-cycles; S all vertices gives only perfect matchings at the Moore-boundary order ten. All types attain five. Two independently constructed exhaustive checkers agree on every size <=5 candidate for three canonical graphs; they confirm examples, not the general proof.

evidence: The pre-existing local-minimum-degree identity converts f(G)=5 to delta_loc(G)=4; it does not determine f(L(H)) in the cyclically robust cubic family or classify equality.
Došlić proves fullerene cyclic connectivity, which is combined with a newly proved edge-cut parity identity and minimizer classification.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known local-complementation identities, cubic fullerene geometry and cyclic connectivity are explicitly excluded from originality. A nontrivial parity-and-small-cut proof is necessary to obtain the three exclusive equality types, so the result is not an immediate corollary of the checked earlier statements.

evidence: The established identity delta_loc(G)+1=min_{A nonempty}|A union Odd_G(A)| relates the optimization to local complementation; Javelle–Mhalla–Perdrix, arXiv:1204.4564v1, and Cattanéo–Perdrix, arXiv:1503.04702v1, provide the historical framework.
The graph-state stabilizer element indexed by A has support exactly A union Odd(A), an equivalent binary-graph-state formulation.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The new theorem includes an exhaustive minimizer classification for line graphs of cyclically five-edge-connected cubic graphs. Inspected older local-complementation treatments give the general optimization identity and complexity or extremal bounds but no such restricted-family classification; the graph-state formulation is reported explicitly rather than treated as a different novelty claim.

evidence: Direct independently specified finite checks give 33, 21 and 42 size-five witnesses for Petersen, Heawood and dodecahedral base graphs.
The original cubic base graphs and the twelve pentagonal fullerene faces are classical and not new counts.
exact_database_or_table.reasoning: No matching exact table was located in the searches actually run; that negative evidence is not exhaustive novelty proof. The theorem is an infinite-family exact classification, not merely three finite table entries. A specialized unindexed stabilizer weight-enumerator table may nevertheless overlap its examples.

value.rationale: For a substantial natural family, the theorem classifies every optimum configuration, including the precise three equality mechanisms, not only the optimum size. Its fullerene specialization gives a uniform weight-five graph-state stabilizer multiplicity n*3/2+12 and identifies the twelve non-generator minimum supports geometrically as pentagons; this is finer than the known fullerene pentagon/cut facts and can inform sparse graph-state and local-complementation analyses.
